clue.text: He should lose weight more quickly

definitions.meaning: one who goes without food, abstaining to slim down
comparative of a word for rapid

explanation.definitionFit: One who abstains from eating is so called, and the same word is the comparative of swift.

clue.text: Harridan who angled to hook a husband

definitions.text: who angled to hook a husband
definitions.meaning: read whimsically as a woman who went fishing to catch a spouse

explanation.definitionFit: A loud, foul-mouthed market woman, punningly a lady who angled for a spouse.

clue.text: Rises to get stalls in operation

parts.note: stalls and stands are both market booths
up means working, running, as in up and running

explanation.surface: Someone gets up to have market booths working.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to one's feet is to rise.

clue.text: Yeoman officer no longer serving

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
on means on duty, serving

explanation.surface: A Yeoman of the Guard officer who has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yeomen of the Guard are a British royal bodyguard; one of their officers bears this title.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer rank in the British sovereign's royal bodyguard.

clue.text: Bound to get HM a dog

parts.note: a bound is a leap, a spring
Her Majesty is ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to obtain a dog for the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as 'obliged' but is a leap; ER (Elizabeth Regina) stands for Her Majesty.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel breed used for flushing game, named for making birds spring up.

clue.text: Note painter's distress at award ceremony

indicators.note: to distress something is to rough it up, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: the word with its s kept as a letter

explanation.surface: An artist is upset by a message at a prize-giving.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'painter's' is needed in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal handing over of a prize is called this.

clue.text: Longing to see enchanting woman lose her head

indicators.note: losing her head means dropping the first letter

parts.note: a witch casts spells, enchants

explanation.surface: Someone wants to see a sorceress beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A craving or yearning is a synonym.

clue.text: Interrogate European through grated window

parts.note: to grill is to question hard

explanation.surface: Questioning a European through a barred window.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice or set of bars over an opening.

clue.text: Jacket an arbiter always returned

indicators.note: returned means the words for arbiter and always are read backwards

parts.note: ref, short for referee, is an arbiter
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A coat the referee keeps sending back.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, thick double-breasted jacket of the kind sailors wear.

clue.text: Use food enhancers in due time

definitions.meaning: to add salt, pepper and spices to a dish
a fitting period, as in 'all in good time'

explanation.surface: Advice to add flavourings when the moment is right.
explanation.definitionFit: To flavour with spices is one sense; the other is a fitting period, as in 'in its proper time'.

clue.text: Give account of French clerk

parts.note: de is French for of
a scribe is a writing clerk

explanation.surface: Tell the story of a French office worker.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount or depict in words is a synonym.

clue.text: Finish one's sentence in correct style

definitions.meaning: read literally as adding the full point that properly closes a sentence

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for ending something; literally, closing a written sentence with a full point.

clue.text: Spacious area of Ludlow I dearly wish to live in

indicators.note: an area of the phrase is a stretch of its letters lying across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: Someone longs to settle in a roomy part of the Shropshire town of Ludlow.
explanation.walkthrough: Ludlow is a market town in Shropshire, England; the letters run across 'Ludlow I dearly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad and roomy are synonyms.

clue.text: Said the tourist operator was to be ridiculed

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: someone who shows tourists round is a guide

explanation.surface: Someone reports that the tour guide was going to be mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is an old word for to mock or poke fun at.

clue.text: A shade risqué

definitions.meaning: a colour, like navy or azure
smutty or off-colour, as in a saucy joke

explanation.definitionFit: It is a colour, and also slang for smutty or indecent.

clue.text: Summer hazard for ophiophobes

definitions.meaning: read as one who sums, adding figures
ophiophobes fear snakes, so a venomous snake

explanation.definitionFit: One who adds up figures, and Britain's venomous snake, the viper.

clue.text: Bob is a pawnbroker

definitions.meaning: as in 'Bob's your ...', a relative named Bob
old slang for a pawnshop owner

explanation.definitionFit: From 'Bob's your uncle', a relative; also old slang for a pawnshop keeper.

clue.text: Discovered in need and unable to cope

parts.note: found means discovered
wanting means lacking, in need

explanation.surface: Someone was located short of necessities and not managing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means judged and shown inadequate for a task.

clue.text: Trap set in late autumn

parts.note: late means deceased, dead
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A snare laid at the end of autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare in which a heavy weight drops on the prey.

clue.text: Poor turinese in need of sustenance

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters are recast

explanation.surface: A poor person from Turin is hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for hungry or greedy.

clue.text: Golfing scorers must be sober people

parts.note: a tee is golf's starting peg
those who add up totals are totallers

explanation.surface: Golf scorekeepers are required to abstain from drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who abstain from alcohol are by definition sober.

clue.text: Soothsayer said to circumscribe many an English leader

indicators.note: circumscribe means draw a line around, so one word encloses another

parts.note: oral means spoken, said
C, the Roman hundred, stands for many

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A prophet is reported to restrict many English leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet or seer, like the one at Delphi.

clue.text: Communicative faculty needed for discourse

definitions.meaning: an address or talk given to an audience

explanation.definitionFit: The ability to talk, and a formal address to an audience.

clue.text: Transported traitor without money

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the traitor word goes round

parts.note: a rat is a traitor or informer
p, penny, is a unit of money

explanation.surface: A turncoat was deported with no cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Enraptured and carried away with delight are synonyms.

clue.text: Where racegoers get salts, maybe

parts.note: a Surrey town famous both for a racecourse hosting the Derby and for its bitter mineral salts

explanation.surface: A punter needing smelling salts at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: The town in Surrey, England, hosts the Derby horse race and gave its name to magnesium sulphate bath salts.
explanation.definitionFit: A Surrey racecourse town whose spring water gave its name to a laxative salt.

clue.text: Polish banker offers nothing to the German

parts.note: nought, the letter O
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A Polish financier puts up zero for the German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a river (it has banks); this one forms part of the Polish-German border.
explanation.definitionFit: A river flowing through Poland, a banker in crossword language.

clue.text: Go crazy on return

indicators.note: on return means the word for crazy is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Turning mad when you come back.
explanation.definitionFit: A go or attempt, as in 'have a go'.

clue.text: Her children are graduates

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts graduate
an MA is a Master of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: A mother proud that her children have degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is whimsical: the woman whose children have the word for her.
explanation.definitionFit: What her offspring call their mother.

clue.text: A citroën modified in production

indicators.note: modified means changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French car altered on the assembly line.
explanation.definitionFit: Making or producing something is a synonym.

clue.text: Virginia heartens wise man of violent nature

indicators.note: read as puts heart into, so the state abbreviation goes in the middle

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A Virginian encourages a fierce old wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce and brutal are synonyms.

clue.text: Old pieces found among his displays

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: found among means placed inside the following word

parts.note: a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: Antique items turned up in his collection of exhibits.
explanation.definitionFit: Items put on show are synonymous with displays.

clue.text: Scoundrel offers inferior item for sale

parts.note: bad means poor, inferior
a lot is an item at auction

explanation.surface: A rogue offers a shoddy auction item.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a rogue or ne'er-do-well.
